title: Coefficient reduction of the Tate Gauss unit ball
statement:
Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value, and put $V=\{a\in K:|a|\le1\}$ and $\mathfrak m=\{a\in K:|a|<1\}$. Then $V$ is a local subring of $K$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and $k=V/\mathfrak m$ is a field; write $a\mapsto ar a$ for its residue map. For $r\ge0$, let $T_r=K\langle X_1,\ldots,X_rangle$ be the restricted-series ring [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], with $\|\sum_
u c_
u X^
u\|_G=\sup_
u|c_
u|$. Put $U_r=\{f\in T_r:\|f\|_G\le1\}$. This is a unital subring, and the assignment $\operatorname{red}:U_r	o k[X_1,\ldots,X_r]$, $\sum_
u c_
u X^
u\mapsto\sum_
u ar c_
u X^
u$, is a well-defined surjective unital ring homomorphism to the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Its kernel is exactly $\{f\in U_r:\|f\|_G<1\}$. It sends a constant $a\in V$ to the constant polynomial $ ar a$. The assertions include $r=0$ and trivial absolute values; completeness is not required.

proof.text: The absolute-value axioms give $|0|=0$, $|1|=|-1|=1$, $|-a|=|a|$, $|ab|=|a||b|$ and $|a+b|\le\max(|a|,|b|)$. Consequently $0,1\in V$, $-V\subset V$, $V+V\subset V$ and $VV\subset V$, so $V$ is a unital subring of $K$. Likewise $0\in\mathfrak m$, $-\mathfrak m\subset\mathfrak m$, and $a,b\in\mathfrak m$ imply $|a+b|<1$; if $a\in\mathfrak m$ and $b\in V$, then $|ab|\le|a|<1$. Thus $\mathfrak m$ is an ideal of $V$, proper because $1\notin\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Bosch, Lectures on Formal and Rigid Geometry (April 2008), Section 1.2, printed pp.8–9 (PDF pp.9–10): coefficient description and Gauss norm, then the reduction paragraph before Proposition 3. Online primary PDF read by Q36 on 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: If $a\in V\setminus\mathfrak m$, then $|a|=1$, so $a\ne0$ and its field inverse has $|a^{-1}|=1$ and belongs to $V$. An element of $\mathfrak m$ cannot be a unit in $V$, since $ab=1$ with $b\in V$ would give $1=|ab|\le|a|<1$. Hence every proper ideal of $V$ is contained in $\mathfrak m$, and any ideal strictly containing $\mathfrak m$ contains a unit and is all of $V$. This proves that $V$ is local, meaning that $\mathfrak m$ is its unique maximal ideal.

proof.text: Apply the quotient-ring construction of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] to $V$ and its ideal $\mathfrak m$ (as a $V$-algebra via the identity). It gives a surjective unital ring map $q:V\to k=V/\mathfrak m$ with kernel $\mathfrak m$. In particular $q(1)\ne0$. Each nonzero class $q(a)$ has $a\notin\mathfrak m$ and inverse $q(a^{-1})$ by step 2. Thus $k$ is a field, and $q(a)=0$ exactly when $|a|<1$. Write $q(a)=\bar a$.

proof.text:
For $f=\sum_
u c_
u X^
u\in T_r$, the cofinite convergence in [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation] says that $S_\epsilon(f)=\{
u:|c_
u|\ge\epsilon\}$ is finite for each real $\epsilon>0$. In particular all coefficient norms are bounded above by $B=\max(\{1\}\cup\{|c_
u|:
u\in S_1(f)\})$. The range of coefficient norms is nonempty (the zero multi-index exists also for $r=0$), so its real supremum is finite. By the defining property of a supremum, $\|f\|_G\le1$ if and only if $|c_
u|\le1$ for every $
u$.

proof.text:
The restricted-series ring is a subring of the formal series ring by [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]. Thus for $f,g\in U_r$ their sum, negative and product already belong to $T_r$. The preceding coefficient criterion puts $0,1,-f,f+g$ in $U_r$. For the product, the Cauchy coefficient is $(fg)_
u=\sum_{\alpha+ eta=
u}c_\alpha d_ eta$; this sum is finite since $0\le\alpha_i\le
u_i$ for all $1\le i\le r$. Every summand has absolute value at most one. Induction on the number of summands using $|a+b|\le\max(|a|,|b|)$ (the empty sum has norm zero) bounds this coefficient by one. Thus $fg\in U_r$ and $U_r$ is a unital subring.

proof.text:
For $f\in U_r$ every $c_
u$ lies in $V$. Step 3 shows that $ ar c_
u
e0$ implies $|c_
u|\ge1$, so the nonzero reduced coefficients are supported on the finite set $S_1(f)$ of step 4. The finite-coefficient description of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] therefore defines the polynomial $\operatorname{red}(f)=\sum_
u ar c_
u X^
u$. Its coefficients prescribe it uniquely; the expression is independent of the finite set used to contain its support.

source.place: Bosch, Lectures on Formal and Rigid Geometry (April 2008), Section 1.2, printed pp.8–9 (PDF pp.9–10): coefficient description and Gauss norm, then the reduction paragraph before Proposition 3. Online primary PDF read by Q36 on 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text:
Addition of series and of polynomials is coefficientwise, and $q$ preserves addition and zero. Hence $\operatorname{red}(f+g)=\operatorname{red}(f)+\operatorname{red}(g)$ and $\operatorname{red}(0)=0$. For each multi-index $
u$, the finite Cauchy formula of step 5 and the quotient ring homomorphism give
$$\overline{(fg)_
u}=q\!\left(\sum_{\alpha+ eta=
u}c_\alpha d_ etaight)=\sum_{\alpha+ eta=
u} ar c_\alpha ar d_ eta.$$
The last expression is exactly the coefficient of the polynomial product $\operatorname{red}(f)\operatorname{red}(g)$ by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Equality of all coefficients proves multiplicativity. The only nonzero coefficient of $1$ is its constant coefficient $1$, and $q(1)=1$, so $\operatorname{red}(1)=1$. This proves that $\operatorname{red}$ is a unital ring homomorphism.

proof.text:
Given a polynomial $P=\sum_{
u\in S}b_
u X^
u$ with $S$ finite, choose for each of its finitely many coefficients a lift $a_
u\in V$ under the surjection $q$. The finite series $f=\sum_{
u\in S}a_
u X^
u$ is restricted: outside $S$ all coefficients are zero. All coefficients have norm at most one, so $f\in U_r$, and its reduction is $P$. Thus $\operatorname{red}$ is surjective, including for $P=0$ by the empty lift. A constant series $a\in V$ has reduction the constant polynomial $ ar a$ by its coefficients.

source.place: Bosch, Lectures on Formal and Rigid Geometry (April 2008), Section 1.2, printed pp.8–9 (PDF pp.9–10): coefficient description and Gauss norm, then the reduction paragraph before Proposition 3. Online primary PDF read by Q36 on 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text:
By equality of polynomial coefficients and $\ker q=\mathfrak m$, one has $\operatorname{red}(f)=0$ if and only if $|c_
u|<1$ for every $
u$. If $\|f\|_G<1$, this follows from $|c_
u|\le\|f\|_G$. Conversely assume every $|c_
u|<1$. The set $S_{1/2}(f)$ is finite, so
$$M=\max igl(\{1/2\}\cup\{|c_
u|:
u\in S_{1/2}(f)\} igr)<1.$$
Outside that set the coefficient norms are less than $1/2$, and inside they are at most $M$; therefore every coefficient norm is at most $M$, and $\|f\|_G\le M<1$. This proves the asserted kernel equality without assuming that the supremum of an arbitrary family of numbers less than one is less than one.

proof.text: All sums used for the ring-map calculation are finite sums in individual coefficients, and the bounds in steps 4 and 9 use only cofinite convergence, so no completeness was used. If $r=0$, the multi-index set has one element and the constructions reduce to $V\to V/\mathfrak m$. For a trivial absolute value, restrictedness at $\epsilon=1$ forces finite support, $V=K$, $\mathfrak m=0$, and the reduction is the identity on polynomials after the canonical identification $K/(0)=K$; the open unit ball consists of the zero series. Thus both stated edge cases are included.

lean.statement: theorem tateUnitBallPolynomialReduction (K : Type u) [NormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] (r : ℕ) : ∃ V : Subring K, (∀ a : K, a ∈ V ↔ ‖a‖ ≤ 1) ∧ IsLocalRing V ∧ ∃ m : Ideal V, (∀ a : V, a ∈ m ↔ ‖(a : K)‖ < 1) ∧ m.IsMaximal ∧ IsField (V ⧸ m) ∧ ∃ U : Subring (MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ (1 : ℝ))), (∀ f : MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ (1 : ℝ)), f ∈ U ↔ MvPowerSeries.gaussNorm (norm : K → ℝ) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ 1) f.val ≤ 1) ∧ ∃ red : U →+* MvPolynomial (Fin r) (V ⧸ m), Function.Surjective red ∧ (∀ (f : U) (ν : Fin r →₀ ℕ), ∃ a : V, (a : K) = MvPowerSeries.coeff ν f.val.val ∧ MvPolynomial.coeff ν (red f) = Ideal.Quotient.mk m a) ∧ (∀ f : U, f ∈ RingHom.ker red ↔ MvPowerSeries.gaussNorm (norm : K → ℝ) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ 1) f.val.val < 1) ∧ (∀ a : V, ∃ f : U, f.val = constants K r (a : K) ∧ red f = MvPolynomial.C (Ideal.Quotient.mk m a))
